SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 2-day history of constant, gradually worsening burning pain below the umbilicus; tender on self-palpation.
- Associated symptoms:
  • Pink-tinged urine; increased urinary frequency without dysuria.  
  • Mild nausea; no vomiting.  
  • Felt hot/sweaty; temperature not measured.  
  • Recent constipation resolved; current bowel motions normal.  
  • Denies diarrhea, shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, visual changes.
- Gynecologic/sexual history:
  • Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse 4 days ago.  
  • On etonogestrel implant (Implanon) ×1 year; still menstruating; last period ≈2 weeks ago.  
  • Last STI screen 6 months ago (normal).  
  • Pregnancy possible though unlikely; no test performed yet.
- Past medical history: None reported; “normally fit and well.”
- Past surgical history: None.
- Medications: 
  • Etonogestrel implant (Implanon).  
  • No other regular medications.
- Social history:
  • Lives in a share house with two roommates.  
  • Occupation: Accountant.  
  • Non-smoker; drinks alcohol socially.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No in-person examination performed (telehealth).  
- No vitals available.
- Investigations: None performed today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with pink urine
   - Likely diagnosis: Uncomplicated urinary tract infection.
   - Differential: Gastrointestinal etiology (e.g., gastritis, early appendicitis), gynecologic causes, early pregnancy-related pathology.
   - Investigations planned: None today; patient advised to obtain home urine dipstick and/or formal urinalysis if no improvement.
   - Treatment: Trimethoprim (dose/route/frequency not fully documented; instructed “one tablet twice daily for 3 days”) sent electronically to pharmacy; encourage hydration, cranberry juice, regular acetaminophen for pain.
   - Follow-up: Reassess in a few days or sooner if worsening pain, persistent fever, vomiting, or other concern.

2. Possible early pregnancy
   - Assessment: Pregnancy unlikely but not excluded (etonogestrel implant in situ).
   - Investigations planned: Home urine pregnancy test; perform promptly.
   - Treatment: None at present.
   - Follow-up: If positive, notify clinic immediately for further care.

3. Patient education / safety-netting
   - Provided red-flag advice: escalating abdominal pain, measured fever, vomiting, hematuria, dysuria, or lack of improvement → seek urgent review.
   - Advised adequate oral fluids and rest.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: allergy status unknown; no objective vitals or abdominal examination due to telehealth setting; medication reconciliation limited to patient report.  
● No internal transcript conflicts noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; occasional minor pauses but clinically adequate.
